glossary.intestinal obstruction: A blockage stopping bowel contents passing along the gut.
glossary.nursing home resident: Someone living in long-term care, often frail and immobile.
glossary.chronic constipation: Long-standing infrequent or difficult passing of stool.
glossary.mobile bowel segment: A loop of bowel that is loosely attached so it can move and twist.
glossary.distension: Swelling of the abdomen from gas or dilated bowel.
glossary.electrolyte abnormalities: Abnormal blood salts such as sodium or potassium, often from vomiting and fluid shifts.
glossary.large bowel obstruction: Blockage of the colon, giving distension, constipation and late vomiting.
glossary.small bowel obstruction: Blockage of the small intestine, giving early vomiting and colicky pain.
glossary.right iliac fossa: The right lower part of the abdomen (RIF).
glossary.right lower quadrant: The lower right area of the abdomen, where the caecum lies.
glossary.sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction from the body's response to infection.
glossary.CT abdomen: A cross-sectional X-ray scan of the abdomen.
glossary.sigmoidoscopy: Looking into the rectum and sigmoid colon with a scope.
glossary.primary anastomosis: Joining two bowel ends together at the same operation.
glossary.colostomy: An opening of the colon onto the abdominal wall.
glossary.resection: Surgical removal of a section of bowel.
glossary.fixation: Surgically anchoring the bowel so it cannot twist again.
glossary.emergency laparotomy: An urgent operation opening the abdomen.
glossary.midline laparotomy: Opening the abdomen through a vertical cut down the middle.
glossary.bowel compromise: Bowel whose blood supply is failing, so it may be dying.
glossary.caecum: The first pouch of the large bowel, in the right lower abdomen.
glossary.axis: The line around which the bowel twists.
glossary.mesenteric attachment: Where the mesentery joins the back of the abdominal wall; narrow bases twist easily.
glossary.mesenteric blood supply: The arteries and veins running in the mesentery to feed the bowel.
glossary.luminal obstruction: Blockage of the inside channel of the bowel.
glossary.institutionalised: Living in long-term care, such as a nursing home.
glossary.immobile: Unable to move about much, which slows the bowel.
glossary.open-loop obstruction: A blockage with only one end closed, so contents can back up.
glossary.mesenteric fold: The line of the twisted mesentery seen running down the middle of the coffee bean.
glossary.comma-shaped: Curved like a comma, describing the dilated caecum.
glossary.fever: Body temperature above about 38 degrees C.
